instructions: Set the bar across the upper back, not the neck, and grip it firmly with the elbows down.

instructions: Lie on a flat bench with the eyes under the bar and the feet flat on the floor.

Press back up until the arms are straight, keeping the shoulder blades set.

main_workout.coaching_cue: Bar to the belly button. If the torso rises to meet it, the weight is winning.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip just outside the knees.
Push the hips back and hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees, keeping the spine long and the knees soft.
Let the bar hang at arm's length, then pull it to the navel by driving the elbows back.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top without letting the torso rise to meet the bar.
Lower the bar under control until the arms are straight and the shoulder blades travel forward.

instructions: Start in a push-up position with the hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line.

main_workout.coaching_cue: Soft knees, long spine, hips travel back — this is a hamstring movement, not a squat.
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell at arm's length against the thighs, hands just outside the knees.
Set the knees softly bent and hold that bend throughout — this is a hinge, not a squat.
Push the hips back and let the bar travel down the front of the legs, keeping the spine long.
Stop when the hamstrings run out of length, usually around mid-shin.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, keeping the bar against the legs the whole way.

main_workout.coaching_cue: Underhand grip brings the biceps in, which is why it is the easier of the two.
instructions: Take an underhand grip on a bar, hands roughly shoulder-width apart.
Hang at full arm extension with the shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
Pull the elbows down to the ribs until the chin clears the bar.

Lower under control all the way to straight arms.

Walk the feet out until the body is straight and the arms are extended.
Pull the chest to the bar, leading with the elbows and keeping the hips level.
Lower under control until the arms are straight again.

vyayama_shakti.principle: Exercise should be performed only to Ardhabala — half of one's maximum capacity (Charaka Sutrasthana 7). It describes the whole session, not a single set: the classical signal that the dose has been reached is sweat on the forehead, nose and joints together with the onset of mouth-breathing.
vyayama_shakti.your_capacity: Keep well inside Ardhabala. Each set should end with two reps still in you, and the session as a whole should leave you with energy to spare. If the classical sign — sweat on the forehead, nose and joints together with breathing through the mouth — arrives before the session's end, stop there and skip what is left. Vata constitution, a beginner's strength and older age all lower exercise tolerance, and over-exertion here depletes Ojas directly.
vyayama_shakti.signs_adequate: Sweat on forehead, nose and armpits; lightness in the body; comfortably increased breathing.
vyayama_shakti.signs_overexertion: Breathlessness, dizziness, tremor, excessive thirst, joint pain or cough mark Ativyayama (over-exercise) — reduce intensity immediately.
vyayama_shakti.bala_note: Exercise capacity (Bala) here is estimated from fitness level and age as a practical proxy — not a full classical Bala Pareeksha, which also weighs Sara, Samhanana, Satmya, Sattva, and season.
